issues: Image 1 failed validation: Image failed editorial review: ["The brief requires a small one-word label beneath each outline (oval, round, square, oblong, heart, diamond, triangle), but the image contains no labels at all, so readers cannot tell which shape is which.","The face shapes are not clearly distinguishable: several faces (e.g., the 1st, 2nd, 6th and 7th) look very similar, and the diamond and triangle shapes are not distinct or recognizable.","The faces are rendered as filled illustrations with hair, eyes, brows and lips rather than minimal smooth line-drawn outlines, adding detail beyond the brief.","Because of missing labels and weak shape differentiation, the image fails to serve its purpose of giving a quick visual overview of the seven face shapes."]

Why "Seven" Is a Convention: The arXiv paper's 2014 study proposed five new categories (kite, rectangle, teardrop, heptagon, oblong), and the draft repeats this. But "oblong" already sits among the paper's five basic shapes, so the claim of five extra categories is internally inconsistent and needs correcting or removing.
